item.aggregated_output:
--- name: data-social-cards description: >- Render publication-grade social images (LinkedIn/X/Instagram) for data findings by generating them programmatically from the snapshot JSON, so no figure in an image is ever hand-typed. Covers the data-vs-generated split, sourcing brand tokens from the repo, headless rendering on AX41, the render-bug checklist, and assembling an approval board. Use whenever a chart, statistic, or dataset finding needs to become a social image or a slide - and specifically whenever tempted to ask an image model for a chart. --- # Data Social Cards ## The one rule **An image model never renders the data. Ever.** Image generation cannot produce exact figures, correct axis positions, or a line whose shape matches a series. It produces something that looks like a chart. The entire credibility of a data post is that every figure is verifiable, so a generated chart destroys the thing the post exists to do. The split that works: | Layer | How | Why | |---|---|---| | Numbers, axes, lines, bars, labels | rendered from the snapshot JSON | correct by construction | | Ground texture, atmosphere, illustrative imagery with no information in it | image model | this is what it is genuinely good at | Generated texture underneath rendered type is a real upgrade over a flat fill and costs nothing in accuracy. Use it. Just keep it under the data, never as the data. ## 1. Read the numbers, do not retype them The generator script opens the snapshot and indexes it. Every figure printed on a card, including the ones inside headline and subtitle strings, is an f-string interpolation. ```py S = json.load(open('snapshot-2026-09.json')) IND = {r['year']: r for r in S['industry_by_year']} sub = (f'Consumer companies: {IND[2014]["Consumer"]}% of the 2014 batch, ' f'{IND[2026]["Consumer"]}% of 2026.') ``` If a number appears as a literal anywhere in the script, that is a bug. The point is not convenience, it is that the card and the report page cannot disagree, and next month's refresh re-renders correctly with no edits. The one legitimate exception is a figure computed in the analysis but not stored in the snapshot. Add it to the snapshot rather than typing it in. ## 2. Take the palette from the codebase, not from taste If the piece belongs to a product, open its stylesheet and read the actual token values. Do not eyeball the brand colour from a screenshot and do not invent a palette next to one that already exists. ```bash sed -n '/^:root/,/^}/p' frontend/app/globals.css # light tokens sed -n '/^\.dark/,/^}/p' frontend/app/globals.css # dark tokens ``` Map them to semantic names in the generator so the intent is legible and a rebrand is one edit: ```py INK, PAPER, MUTE = '#0A0A0A', '#FFFFFF', '#A3A3A3' # --rl-bg / --rl-text / --rl-subtle BRAND = '#F94F00' # --rl-accent ALIVE = '#34D399' # --rl-success EXITED = '#F59E0B' # --rl-score-medium ``` **Spend the brand hue on the series the post is about.** A green/amber/red traffic light is semantically tidy and reads as a generic chart with no owner. Putting the brand colour on the one series the headline names, and leaving the rest quiet, makes it the product's chart. Concentrate boldness in one place. ## 3. Format - **LinkedIn portrait 1080 × 1350 (4:5)** is the default: maximum vertical feed space. Square 1080 × 1080 only when the composition genuinely wants it. - PNG for upload (crisp type), max 8MB. A JPEG copy at ~900px is for previews only. - One idea per card. A card that needs a second chart is a second post. Structure that holds up at feed size: mono eyebrow, large display headline with the key phrase in the brand colour, a two-or-three-line mono subtitle carrying the exact figures, the chart, then a rule and a footer with source and URL. The headline is read at thumbnail size; the chart is read after the tap. ## 4. Render headless on AX41, never on the Mac ```bash ssh ax41 'sudo mkdir -p /root/' tar cf - card-*.html | ssh ax41 'sudo tar xf - -C /root/' ssh ax41 'sudo bash -c "cd /root/ && for f in card-*.html; do timeout 90 google-chrome-stable --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --hide-scrollbars \ --window-size=1080,1350 --screenshot=\"\${f%.html}.png\" --virtual-time-budget=8000 \ \"file:///root//\$f\"; done"' ssh ax41 'sudo tar cf - -C /root/ card-a.png card-b.png' | tar xf - ``` Notes that save a debugging round: - `--window-size` must equal the card's CSS pixel size exactly; do not rely on scaling. - `--virtual-time-budget=8000` gives webfonts time to land. Too low and the card renders in the fallback stack, which looks fine in a thumbnail and wrong at full size. - Keep the generated texture as a sibling file referenced relatively. Rendering happens next to it, so there is no need to inline it as a data URI. - If a card comes back blank or half-painted, that is the known headless rAF stall - force `Page.captureScreenshot` over CDP instead of the `--screenshot` flag. - ImageMagick is not reliably present. For downscaling on the Mac use the built-in: `sips -Z 900 -s format jpeg -s formatOptions 78 in.png --out out.jpg` ## 5. Look at every image before showing it Read the rendered PNG. Every card, every re-render. Do not ship a card you have not viewed; the whole point of rendering deterministically is lost if nobody checks the render. These four bugs appeared in a single first pass and all four are invisible in source: | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Axis shows `%` with no number | label drawn at `x < 0`, clipped by the viewBox | left padding must exceed the widest label, not the tick | | Two segment labels overlap | per-segment labels under a stacked bar of varying widths | one legend row above; never label narrow segments in place | | Big empty band under the chart | SVG `height` larger than its drawn content, centred by flex | set the viewBox height to the actual content height | | First data point has no tick label | `if year % 2 == 0` skips an odd first year | `if y % 2 == 0 or y in (years[0], years[-1])` | Then check: does the last point's value label match the snapshot, does the axis maximum clip any series, is the headline legible at 25% zoom. ## 6. Generated ground Ask for texture, not content. Enumerate the exclusions explicitly - image models add text and chart-like marks unprompted, and any of those under a real chart is a credibility problem. > Abstract editorial background texture for a data-journalism poster. Neutral charcoal > near-black ground, no green and no blue cast, a faint warm tint upper left only. Faint > hand-drawn ledger grid lines and worn graph-paper rules, uneven ink density, subtle paper > fibre and risograph grain. Soft diagonal light from the upper left. Extremely low contrast, > muted, restrained. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no charts, no logos, no people. Composite with a scrim so contrast never depends on the generated pixels: ```css background: linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(10,10,10,.55) 0%, rgba(10,10,10,.86) 55%, rgba(10,10,10,.94) 100%), #0A0A0A url('bg-texture.png') center/cover no-repeat; ``` Match the texture's colour cast to the brand ground. A pine-green texture under a neutral near-black palette reads as a mismatch immediately. On AX41, Codex's built-in image generation works through its ChatGPT OAuth session with no API key. `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-rules "Generate one image … and save it to /root//bg-texture.png at 1088x1360"`. Size constraints for gpt-image models: each edge a multiple of 16, ratio ≤ 3:1, total pixels between 655,360 and 8,294,400. The standalone `image_gen.py` fallback needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` and will fail without one; going through `codex exec` does not. ## 7. Approval board Never post directly from the render. Assemble one self-contained HTML page pairing each post's copy with its card, and publish it for review: ```bash cat board.html | openhtmlfeedback --title "…" --project

--agent claude \ --replace-key "::drafts" ``` `--replace-key` updates the same card on re-render instead of piling up. Embed the JPEG previews as base64 data URIs so the page is self-contained. Put on the board, next to each post: the first two lines isolated (all that shows before "see more"), word and character count, and any blocker that must clear before it can go out (a link target that is not live yet, an approval outstanding). The board is where the blockers get seen, so state them, do not assume they are remembered. Nothing is scheduled or posted from this skill. Copy and visuals get approved first. ## See also - `public-dataset-report` - producing the snapshot these cards read from, and killing the findings that should never reach a card. - `linkedin-native-founder-posts` - the copy that goes beside the visual.

The surprising weakness is Research verification: despite only three research entries, one explicitly reports a prior failure to verify a source; Visual design is more severe overall because two of four entries contain direct corrective feedback.
Both deliverables are drafted. I’m now validating the JSON schema/content, scanning both outputs for prohibited source details, and rendering the SVG for a final visual check.
